subject: Order Form: subrogation & escrow trigger sequencing / defense allocation
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@acmelegal.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form – sequence for subrogation / escrow triggers and defense allocation

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal is reviewing the order form and a few commercial questions came up we wanted to resolve before legal completes procurement review. Two items we need clarity on:

1) Subrogation & escrow trigger: our procurement team prefers an escrow trigger tied to a higher threshold (e.g., losses > $250k) rather than immediate escrow or holdback on first notice of claim. Can Redwood confirm whether we can: (a) limit escrow triggers to final judgments or settlements over $250k, or (b) alternatively accept an insurance-credit mechanism (i.e., Redwood's insurance pays first, with subrogation rights preserved)?

2) Defense allocation if the claim implicates model output and third-party IP: Acme is asking for the right to control defense for customer-originated takedown claims where technical evidence shows the output came from our prompt and dataset. Redwood has previously pushed for defend-and-control for third-party IP. Is there flexibility for a hybrid approach (Acme takes control for customer-provided-prompt claims; Redwood controls defense for model-internal claims)?

I've attached Acme's commented order form (Acme_Commented_OrderForm.docx). Can you loop in your legal team and let us know Redwood's preferred sequencing and a practicable fallback for procurement's review?

Appreciate a quick turn–Acme hopes to finalize the PO by end of week.

Best,
Amanda

Subject: Re: Order Form – sequence for subrogation / escrow triggers and defense allocation

Amanda — thanks for the clear asks and the annotated doc. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Connor (ops/tech evidence) to propose language and operational constraints.

Quick summary of how we can approach this so procurement has workable options:

- Escrow / insurance credit: Redwood prefers an insurance-first approach where our commercial insurance responds to covered claims, and subrogation rights remain. If Acme needs an escrow, we can agree to an escrow trigger but suggest tying it to: (i) final judgment or settlement > $200,000 OR (ii) written admission of liability by Redwood. That keeps small triage claims out of escrow and aligns with our insurance retention.

- Defense allocation: We can accept a hybrid carve where Acme controls defense for claims where: (a) Acme's customer prompt/inputs can be demonstrated to be the proximate cause of the output (per provided evidence), AND (b) the claim is limited to that customer's use case. Redwood retains defend-and-control for third-party claims tied to the model's training data or model architecture. For overlap, we propose a short dispute-escalation window (5 business days) where parties attempt to agree on control before defaulting to an independent counsel appointment process.

Kimberly — can you propose specific redline text for the order form (escrow trigger thresholds + insurance-credit clause + the hybrid defense-control paragraph)? Connor — can you confirm what evidence metadata and retention windows we can commit to for Acme to validate prompt causation (logs, timestamped inputs, model-version ids, etc.).

I will keep Acme in the loop and mark this high priority — they need language for procurement by EOW.

Thanks,
Rachel

Subject: Re: Order Form – sequence for subrogation / escrow triggers and defense allocation

Rachel/Amanda — thanks for the framing. Below are proposed redlines and operational notes. I've kept the language as procurement-friendly as possible while protecting Redwood's indemnity exposure and insurer relationships.

1) Escrow / Insurance-credit language (new section in Order Form):
Proposed: "If a Third-Party Claim results in a final judgment or settlement against Redwood in excess of Two Hundred Thousand Dollars ($200,000), Redwood shall, within thirty (30) days of such final judgment or settlement, (a) satisfy the judgment or settlement through its available insurance or cash resources, and (b) if Redwood's available insurance proceeds are insufficient to satisfy such judgment or settlement, Redwood shall deposit into escrow an amount equal to the shortfall. Escrow deposits shall not be required based solely on notice of a claim, investigation, or non-final determination."

Commentary: This preserves the insurance-first model and avoids escrow on unproven notices. It also maps to common procurement concerns while keeping exposure bounded.

2) Insurance-credit / offsets (clause):
Proposed: "Redwood's indemnity obligations shall be reduced by any amounts paid under Redwood's insurance proceeds applicable to the Claim. To the extent Redwood receives insurance proceeds, Redwood shall notify Customer and apply such proceeds to satisfy Redwood's indemnity obligations before any escrow deposit is required."

3) Hybrid defense-control carve (new paragraph in Indemnity):
Proposed: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assume control of the defense of a Claim alleging that Customer-provided inputs (including prompts, instructions, or data supplied by Customer) caused the generation of infringing output, provided that Customer: (a) produces demonstrable metadata and logs reasonably sufficient to show such causal linkage, (b) assumes all costs and indemnity obligations arising solely from such defended claims, and (c) coordinates with Redwood on joint settlements that materially affect Redwood's rights. For Claims that implicate Redwood's model training data or proprietary model architecture, Redwood shall retain the right to assume defense and control. In cases of disputed allocation, Parties shall engage an independent technical reviewer within five (5) business days; the reviewer’s determination as to evidentiary linkage will be binding for defense-allocation purposes."

Operational asks for Connor: please confirm we can commit to retaining timestamped request logs, model-version id, and response snapshots for 12 months, and provide a process for producing them under a standard evidence request with an SLA (e.g., 5 business days for triage, 15 days for full dataset export). If we cannot meet 12 months retention, propose alternative (e.g., 6 months + archive on request).

If Acme agrees to the threshold ($200k) and the independent reviewer process, I think procurement will have a path to sign. Happy to iterate on wording.

Kim

Two quick confirmations before we route to PO: 
- Evidence retention: Acme accepts 12 months of timestamped request logs + model-version ids and a 15 business-day full export SLA.
- DocuSign path: Procurement will sign once Redwood provides the final redline in PDF and we receive a DocuSign envelope for the Order Form + attached SOW.

We appreciate the collaborative approach — looks like a path to close this week.
